facts.statement: The name Melanorosaurus means "Black Mountain Lizard" derived from Greek words for black, mountain, and lizard.
facts.quote: Melanorosaurus (meaning "Black Mountain Lizard", from the Greek melas/, "black", oros/, "mountain" + /, "lizard")

facts.statement: Melanorosaurus was an omnivore from South Africa with a large body and sturdy limbs that suggest it moved on all fours.
facts.quote: An omnivore from South Africa, it had a large body and sturdy limbs, suggesting it moved quadrupedally.

facts.statement: The skull of Melanorosaurus measured approximately 250 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: Melanorosaurus had a skull which measured approximately 250 mm.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Melanorosaurus had four teeth on each side, a trait characteristic of primitive sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: The premaxilla had four teeth on each side, a characteristic of primitive sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Melanorosaurus was around 8 meters long and weighed approximately 1.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Melanorosaurus was around 8 m long, with a weight of 1.3 MT.

facts.statement: The type specimens of Melanorosaurus were discovered, described, and named in 1924 by Sidney H. Haughton.
facts.quote: The type specimens, syntypes SAM-PK-3449 and SAM-PK-3450, were discovered, described and named in 1924 by Sidney H. Haughton.

facts.statement: Melanorosaurus fossils were collected from the Lower Elliot Formation dating to the early Norian on the north slope of the Black Mountain in Transkei, South Africa.
facts.quote: They were collected from the Triassic Lower Elliot Formation, dating to the early Norian, on the north slope of the Thaba 'Nyama (Black Mountain) in Transkei, South Africa.

facts.statement: In 2024, Melanorosaurus was redescribed and the specimen SAM-PK-3449 was designated as the lectotype.
facts.quote: In 2024, Melanorosaurus was redescribed and SAM-PK-3449 was designated the lectotype of the species.

facts.statement: The first complete skull referred to Melanorosaurus, cataloged as NM QR3314, was described in 2007.
facts.quote: The first complete skull referred to Melanorosaurus, NM QR3314, was described in 2007.

facts.statement: The first skull of Melanorosaurus was not described until 2007, when it was cataloged under the inventory number NM QR3314.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 2007 cuando el primer cráneo de Melanorosaurus fue descrito, catalogado bajo el número de inventario NM QR3314.

facts.statement: A recent review demonstrated that the femur and six other bones attributed to Melanorosaurus thabanensis cannot be referred to the genus, leading to the creation of the new combination Meroktenos thabanensis.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una revisión reciente del material demostró que el fémur, junto con otros seis huesos, no puede ser referido al género Melanorosaurus y se creó la nueva. combinación.

facts.statement: Under some definitions of Sauropoda, Melanorosaurus is classified as an early sauropod.
facts.quote: According to some definitions of Sauropoda, Melanorosaurus is an early sauropod.

facts.statement: Adam Yates has proposed a definition of Sauropoda that specifically excludes Melanorosaurus, defining the group as sauropodomorphs closer to Saltasaurus than to Melanorosaurus.
facts.quote: Adam Yates has proposed a definition of Sauropoda that will specifically exclude Melanorosaurus (Sauropoda as all sauropodomorphs closer to Saltasaurus than Melanorosaurus).

facts.statement: Melanorosaurus was once classified as a prosauropod but is now recognized as one of the earliest sauropods.
facts.quote: Melanorosaurus fue alguna vez clasificado como un prosaurópodo, pero hoy es reconocido como uno de los primeros saurópodos.

facts.statement: Basal sauropods such as Melanorosaurus, Anchisaurus, and Antetonitrus are considered intermediates between prosauropods and true sauropods.
facts.quote: Los saurópodos basales son por ejemplo Melanorosaurus, Anchisaurus y Antetonitrus son intermedios entre estos grupos.

facts.statement: Melanorosaurus readi is the only known species of the extinct genus Melanorosaurus, a melanorosaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago in the Norian stage, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Melanorosaurus readi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Melanorosaurus (gr. "lagarto de la montaña negra") de dinosaurio saurópodo melanorosáurido que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 210 millones de años, en el Noriense, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: This large herbivore from South Africa, measuring around 8 meters long and weighing 1.3 tons, had a large body and robust limbs, suggesting it moved on all fours.
facts.quote: Este gran herbívoro de Sudáfrica, de alrededor de 8 metros de largo y un peso de 1,3 toneladas, tenía un gran cuerpo y los miembros robustos, sugiriendo que se movían sobre sus cuatro patas.

facts.statement: Like most sauropod vertebrae, the vertebrae of Melanorosaurus had hollows that helped reduce weight.
facts.quote: Y como la mayoría de las vértebras de saurópodos, las suyas tenían huecos que ayudaban a reducir el peso.

facts.statement: Prosauropods were once considered ancestral to sauropods, but differences in ankle bone design indicate that they are sister groups.
facts.quote: Los prosaurópodos, alguna vez fueron considerado un conjunto de animales ancestrales a los saurópodos, pero las diferencias en el diseño de sus huesos del tobillo precisan que éstos son grupos hermanos.

facts.statement: The time range for Melanorosaurus spans from the Norian to the Sinemurian, approximately 227.3 to 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Sinemurian (227.3 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The limb bones of Melanorosaurus were massive and heavy, similar to those of true sauropods.
facts.quote: Its limb bones were massive and heavy like the limb bones of true sauropods.

rejected.statement: The maxilla of Melanorosaurus possessed 19 teeth on each side of the jaw.
rejected.quote: The maxilla had 19 teeth on each side of the jaw.

rejected.statement: The specimen SAM-PK-3450 was excluded from Melanorosaurus in 2024 because it differs significantly from the lectotype and is now considered a probable sauropodomorph.
rejected.quote: However, SAM-PK-3450 differs in many aspects from SAM-PK-3449 so was excluded from Melanorosaurus, representing a probable sauropodomorph.

rejected.statement: The referral of the 2007 skull specimen NM QR3314 to Melanorosaurus is considered untenable because it comes from the Upper Elliot Formation, unlike the type material.
rejected.quote: However, this specimen comes from the Upper Elliot, unlike the Melanorosaurus type material and NM QR1551, rendering its referral to the genus untenable.
